name: Wängle
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy village in the Außerfern with an ideal location between Reutte and Lake Plansee.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The sunny municipality of Wängle is situated at 882 metres above sea level in the Außerfern region of Tyrol within the Reutte district, nestling at the foot of the Hahnenkamm mountain. With approximately 950 inhabitants, this charming village sits upon an expansive hillside terrace west of the River Lech, overlooking the valley basin of Reutte. Thanks to its elevated position, Wängle enjoys above-average sunshine and panoramic views extending across the district capital of Reutte, the Ammergau and Lechtal Alps, and the world-renowned Ehrenberg castle ensemble. The municipality encompasses picturesque hamlets including Holz, Niederwängle, and Winkl, making it an ideal destination for travellers who appreciate scenic relaxation paired with diverse mountain sports right next to regional amenities.

Geschichte

Wängle possesses a remarkably ancient and distinguished history. Given its proximity to the Roman trade artery Via Claudia Augusta, the basin was developed in antiquity. As the ancient mother parish of the entire Reutte district, Wängle was documented as early as 1278; for centuries, neighbouring villages such as Reutte, Breitenwang, Lechaschau, and Höfen were ecclesiastical subsidiaries of Wängle. The village's cultural treasure is the Baroque parish church of St. Martin, remodelled around 1730. It houses splendid ceiling frescoes created by the celebrated Tyrolean Baroque master Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–1794), who is buried in the churchyard. Wängle maintained its agrarian traditions until the mid-20th century when cable car development transformed it into a year-round holiday destination.

Anreise

Benefiting from its proximity to the regional hub of Reutte, Wängle enjoys excellent accessibility. By road, motorists arriving from Germany can travel toll-free via the federal highway B179 through the Füssen border tunnel, or from Innsbruck via the Inntal Autobahn A12 and the Fernpass road B179 into Reutte. From the town centre, a short drive across the Lech via Lechaschau on local road L288 ascends to Wängle's plateau. Rail travelers arrive via the Außerfernbahn line at Reutte in Tirol station, where frequent regional buses connect directly to Wängle and the base station of the Hahnenkamm cable car.

Tipps

A premier alpine highlight is the Hahnenkammbahn cable car in neighbouring Höfen-Wängle, whisking hikers and skiers up to 1,730 metres. At the mountain station, visitors will find the Panoramarestaurant Hahnenkamm, an alpine botanical garden, and the barefoot walking trail designed to stimulate the senses across diverse natural surfaces. In winter, the mountain offers family-friendly downhill skiing. Another nearby natural gem is the Frauensee, a peaceful woodland lake with a traditional lakeside inn perfect for relaxing walks. Culturally inclined guests should admire the Zeiller frescoes inside St. Martin's Church and take in vistas of the Ehrenberg castle ruins and the highline179 suspension bridge.
